newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Macau's summer schedule likely to add 50 flights.
newsitem.headline: Macau's summer schedule likely to add 50 flights.

text.p: More than 50 new scheduled flights a week are expected at Macau International Airport when the summer schedule begins on April 1, airport sources said.
The provisional schedule, which is still subject to change, shows that flights will increase from 330 to more than 380 a week, the sources said.

Air Macau, which operates 53 flights a week, is planning to expand its schedule to 83 flights per week, an airline source said. The Portuguese enclave's flag carrier, which has just taken delivery of a new Airbus A321 with another due shortly, is expanding its regional network in China with a new service to Qingdao due to start on March 23.
The carrier is also planning to increase its Shanghai service to twice daily. Additional destinations to Wuhan and Haikou are due to start to in May, the airline source said in an interview.
North Korea's Air Koryo is another carrier which is expected to increase its Macau service, doubling its current once weekly schedule between Pyongyang and Bangkok via Macau.

Earlier this week the airport said February set a new traffic record handling 150,772 passengers making a total since the airport opened in November 1995 of 1.6 million passengers or well ahead of expectations.

Industry sources said Macau is keen to capture as much business as possible before the anticipated start of direct flights between Taiwan and China and before Hong Kong's new, uncongested, 24 hour airport at Chek Lap Kok opens due next year. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
